brief: Little hexagon pieces that snap together and pull apart, for my nine-month-old to play with on the floor.

requirements.evidence: Each Hex base is ~191 mm wide; 3-piece build measures 364 x 467 mm per measure. These are large floor tiles, not little hand-held pieces.

Build uses piece:-1,0,0, 0,0,0, 0,1,0 with solid top covers and end caps, joined as one body with jointBolts (jointBolt:0#-1,0#0, jointBolt:0#0,0#5). Side-connector joining exists in the system but is a rigid printed joint, not a toy snap, and the as-built locked cluster does not pull apart by hand.

check_build ok, meshClash clear, capped faces and locked joints; no props (toy staging not dressed). But configurator checks fit/collisions only and knows nothing about materials, strength, mouthing/chewing, choking, or age safety; parts are 3D printed in user-chosen material. Not verified safe for a 9-month-old, and detachable caps/covers/connectors are not infant-rated.
requirements.requirement: safe for a nine-month-old to play with on the floor

finish.summary: Built a 3-cell large hex tile cluster with solid covers, end caps and locked joints (verified, mesh clear). It shows the hexagon floor-play idea at large scale, but it is not little, does not function as a pull-apart infant snap toy, and infant safety/material suitability is unverified — do not give to a nine-month-old as a toy.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

result.note: A joint bolt fastens the wall between two touching bases. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

A side connector joins two bases that stand side by side on the same storey. Bases that touch with no connector on the wall between them are one body (joint bolts); every wall between two groups needs a connector, walls inside a group stay bare. get_build lists each touching wall and the groups.
